translations.text: A sermon for Palm Sunday by our holy father John Chrysostom. Brothers, we pass from one of the Lord’s miracles to another.
And we advance as though from strength to strength. For just as in golden chains,
the links are intertwined with one another, and each of the intertwined links holds on to another,
each is joined to another, and the chain is extended,
so too the miracles of the holy Gospels follow one another
and gladden Christ’s feast-loving Church with food that does not perish,
but endures to eternal life. So let us too, beloved,
with prepared hearts and ears ready to listen, hear what the Lord, the Lord, says to us
through the prophets and in the Gospels about this holy feast.
For he will indeed speak peace to his people and to his holy ones,
and to those who turn their hearts toward him. Today the prophetic trumpets have stirred the whole world
and have gladdened and adorned the Lord’s churches everywhere.
And, taking over from the toil of holy fasting and the struggle against passion,
they [?] a song of victory and a new composition for the world,
and have taught it to sing to the victorious Christ. Come, then, everyone, let us rejoice in the Lord.
Come, all nations, let us clap our hands and cry out to God our Savior with a joyful voice.
Let no one be deprived of joy; let no one be deprived of the invitation, lest they be like the offspring of the disobedient, destined for destruction.
Let no one be unaware of the king’s arrival, lest they be shut outside the bridal chamber.
Let no one be found sluggish in welcoming him, lest they be condemned with the wicked citizens.
I do not call citizens those who were unwilling to receive their lord and king among them.
Let us all run together with joy; let us all welcome him eagerly.
And let us celebrate beyond this world. Instead of garments, let us spread our hearts before him.
With songs and praises let us give him thanks. “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”
Let us cry out without ceasing, for those who bless him are blessed, while those who curse
him are cursed. Again I will speak, and, striving for what is good, I will not remain silent: come, beloved, let us bless the Blessed One.
May we be blessed by him. He summoned all flesh and every authority together to praise the Lord.
The kings of the earth and all earthly judges, young men and maidens. And a wondrous new marvel:
For the young and inexperienced in evil, the little children still nursing in the flesh, [?] to pray [?] to begin giving thanks to the Lord,
a song taught by God, as Moses once sang for the people coming out of Egypt.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Today blessed David rejoices with joy,
with the children as his beautifully adorned harps, with whom he also dances in spirit.
And rejoicing as he did before, in front of the ark of God, he sings and sweetly proclaims:
“Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.” Let us say to him, “Tell us, O prophet,
who is this who comes in the name of the Lord?” “Today’s teaching is not mine,” he said,
“for it has been granted to the children by him who perfected praise out of the mouths of children and nursing infants,
to destroy the enemy and the avenger, so that through these wonders the hearts of fathers may turn to their children,
and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous.” Speak, O children! Where did you get
these good and joyful words and this song? Who taught you? Who made you wise? Who gathered you together?
Where are the books? Where are the witnesses? “Share in our joy,” they said,
“and learn the song that Moses and the other prophets have in mind.” So, since we have been overcome,
and the children have given us the right hand of fellowship, come, beloved,
let us too eagerly join the dance that rejoices in God, and make a way with the apostles
for him who ascended to the heaven of heavens in the east, and who, as he willed, sits on a donkey’s colt on earth.
Let us take up palm branches with the children, and dance with leafy boughs,
so that he may breathe the Holy Spirit into us too, and let us raise in due order a song taught by God:
“Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the highest!”
Today Jacob, the foremost of the fathers, also celebrates in spirit, seeing his prophecy fulfilled in deed,
and seeing him who ties his colt to the vine mounted on a young colt.
And with the faithful he bows down in spirit. Today the colt is being made ready,
the former senseless unruliness of the irrational nations, as a sign of the submission of the new people from the nations.
And the little children proclaim the infancy of their knowledge of God, and what follows
toward perfection in godliness. Today the King of glory is glorified on earth in the words of the prophets.
And he has made those on earth sharers in heavenly joy,
to show that he is Lord of both, being praised by both
with one voice, together with the Father and the Spirit. For this reason those above,
proclaiming the salvation of those on earth, sang: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts.
Heaven and all the earth are full of his glory.” And those below, with heavenly joy,
celebrating together with heavenly joy, cried out: “Hosanna in the highest!
Hosanna to the Son of David!” And some gave glory, saying: “Blessed is the glory of the Lord from his dwelling place.”
And others spoke of God, saying: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.”
While these things were happening, and the disciples were rejoicing over all the mighty deeds they had seen
and saying, “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory on earth!”
the city was shaken, saying, “Who is this?” It stirred up blind envy against the Master's glory.
When you hear “the city,” understand the disorderly multitude of the old synagogue.
The foolish ask, “Who is he to me?” as though they had never seen the benefactor,
glorious through miracles worthy of God. For the shadow did not comprehend that within it there shone
the undimmed light. Therefore Isaiah had plainly cried out to them beforehand, saying: “You deaf, hear!
And you blind, look up and see! Who is blind but my servants, and deaf
but those who rule over them? And the servants of God have become blind. You have seen many times, but have paid no attention.
Your ears are open, but you have not heard.” Do you see, beloved, the precision of these words,
how God's Holy Spirit, through his holy ones, proclaimed what was to happen as though it had already happened?
For the lawless saw and touched the miracles of God the wonderworker, yet remained in unbelief.
They knew the man blind from birth, who proclaimed as Lord the one who had given him sight.
They saw the paralytic, bound in fetters for many years, freed from his affliction by a command.
They saw Lazarus, who had been [?] of death. They heard of the walking on the sea and the provision of wine without labor.
Feeding with food obtained without labor; driving out demons; healing the sick.
The highways proclaimed his mighty works; the roads proclaimed his healings to travelers.
All Judea was filled with his good deeds. Yet now they ask, “Who is this?”
Oh, the great foolishness of false teachers! Oh, disobedient fathers!
Oh, foolish elders! Oh, shameless offspring of Canaan, and not of blessed Judah [?]!
The children recognized the Creator, but the disobedient fathers said, “Who is this?”
The young and innocent generation praised the Creator, but those who had grown foolish through evil days
asked, “Who is this?” Nursing infants speak of God, but the elders blaspheme. Children reverently offer praise,
but the impure priests are fiercely angry. You who disobey the wisdom of the righteous,
turn to your children. Learn the mysteries of God. What is happening itself bears witness
that the one praised in this way by untaught tongues is God. Search the Scriptures,
as you heard from the Lord, for they bear witness about him.
And do not say, “There were no miracles [?].” Hear, you hard-hearted people, what the prophet Zechariah proclaims to you.
For he said, “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Look, your king comes to you, righteous
and mounted on a young colt.” Why do you cast joy away from yourselves?
Why do you love darkness when the sun is shining? Why do you stir up war against undisturbed peace?
If, then, you are sons of Zion, celebrate with your children. Let a reason for joy be
your children’s reverence for God. Learn from them who taught them,
who gathered them, where their teaching comes from, what this new proclamation of God is,
and this ancient prophecy. But if no human being taught them any of these things,
and they sing praise on their own, recognize the work of God, as it is written in the Law:
“From the mouths of infants and nursing babies you have perfected a song.” Therefore, double your joy,
for you have become servants of such children, who—what was unknown even to the elders—
praised it, taught by God. Turn your hearts toward your children,
and do not close your eyes to the truth. But if you remain the same, then, even though you hear, you do not hear.
Though you see, you do not see. You foolishly rage against the little children, and they will be your judges, according to the Savior’s word.
The prophet Isaiah rightly foretold this too about you, along with other things, saying:
“Jacob will not now be ashamed, nor will his face now change.
But when their children see my works, they will sanctify my name for my sake.
They will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and fear the God of Israel.
Those who have gone astray in spirit will gain understanding, and those who rage will learn to obey.
And mute tongues will learn to speak peace.” Do you see, O unbelieving Jew,
how, from his very first words, the prophet foretells your shame because of your disobedience?
Learn at least from him how he proclaims your children’s song to be taught by God, just as the blessed
David sang beforehand, saying, “From the mouths of little children and nursing infants you have perfected praise.”
Either accept the children’s blessing, as is fitting, or else give us the children together with their devotion. We rejoice together with them.
We celebrate with them and sing a song taught by God in a new tongue.
For once the elder Simeon met the Savior and took into his arms the Creator of the ages
as a little child, and proclaimed him Lord and God. But now, in place of the elder, uncomprehending
children met the Savior as Simeon had, and spread branches in place of his arms.
And they blessed the Lord God, seated on a colt as on a cherub:
“Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”
Let us too sing with them: “Blessed is God who is from God,
the King of glory! O you who became poor [?], though yourself free from poverty, for our sake,
to enrich us with your goodness! Blessed is he who came in humility and comes again in glory:
the first time, meek upon a colt and praised by little children, so that what was written might be fulfilled: ‘Your processions were seen, O God,
the processions of my God, the King who is in the sanctuary’; the second time, coming on the clouds and glorified by angels
and heavenly powers.” O how the children’s tongue drips honey! O how freely given is the teaching
of those who please God! The prophet David hid the meaning beneath the writing, but the children together uncovered it
and brought out its riches on their tongues. With joyful words they eagerly called everyone to be filled.
Let us too, then, draw with them from on high and from the riches of heaven, with insatiable bosoms.
And let us store God's gifts in our homes. Let us cry out unceasingly: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
True God in the name of the Lord, the true God; the almighty Son in the name of the Father.
A true king from a true king, possessing an eternal and everlasting kingdom,
together with the one who begot him, just as the one who begot him does; for their kingdom is shared.
And the Word, the Son, shares in this same honor, not as an outsider. For it neither has a beginning nor increases
or diminishes. Be silent! Rather, it belongs to him by nature and truly in his own right.
For the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit have one kingdom.
Just as there is one kingdom, there is one lordship. Therefore we serve them with one worship.
One Godhead in three persons, without beginning, uncreated, unable to be driven away or changed.
For the Father will never cease to be what he is in his person. For the Trinity suffers no diminution
or ever loses its eternity, its communion, or its kingdom. For it was not because the Son of God became man
and overcame the one who tormented him, accomplishing in the flesh the victory over its evil enemy,
that he became king by accomplishing this. Rather, being king and God, he is therefore king forever,
just like the one who begot him, both now and forever after his birth. Do not blaspheme Christ's kingdom, you blasphemer,
lest you dishonor the one who begot him. If you are a believer,
come faithfully to Christ, our true God, and not like the former one, taking wicked liberties.
But if you are a slave, submit to your master with fear. For one who argues is not a loyal slave,
but plainly an adversary. For it is written: Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
But we, beloved, to the point from which we departed,
let us return in our discourse, crying out: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
The good and kind shepherd will lay down his life for his sheep,
so that, just as hunters use a sheep to lure wolves that prey on sheep,
so the ruler of the flock, setting himself before the intelligent and soul-destroying wolves as a man,
will ensnare those who previously ensnared Adam, on behalf of Adam, who was caught by them.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. God comes against the devil, not openly with invisible
power, but with weak flesh, to bind the one who is powerful against us.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. The King comes against the adversary,
not with the power and wisdom of almighty rule, but through the seeming foolishness of the cross; from the serpent that lives in wickedness
he will plunder its spoils. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. The true one comes against the liar, the Savior
against the destroyer, the peacemaker against the adversary, the lover of humanity against the hater of humanity.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. The Lord will have mercy on his creation.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. The Savior of deceived humanity
will destroy deception, enlighten those in darkness, and abolish the deception of pagan shrines,
and in its place introduce the saving knowledge of God, sanctify the world, and drive out the defilement and shame
of the worship of worthless gods [?]. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
One for many and after many, he will deliver the poor human race from the hands of those stronger than it,
and the poor and needy from those who plunder them. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
He will pour oil and wine on the man who fell among robbers and was left neglected.
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. He will save us himself, as the prophet said:
“Neither an intercessor nor a messenger, but the Lord himself saved them.” Therefore we too bless you, Lord,
with the Father and the Holy Spirit, before the ages and forever and ever,
you who were blessed before the ages and until now without flesh, but now and forever with the holy
incarnation that remains without change and without separation. But let us see next
what the holy Gospel says. When the Lord had entered the temple,
the blind and the lame came to him, and he healed them all. But when the chief priests
and the Pharisees saw the miracles he performed, and the children crying out and saying, “Hosanna
to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”
they could not endure this honor. So they came to him and said, “Do you not hear what these children are saying?
Is it not burdensome for you to be praised? Is it not distressing for you to hear this from innocent children?
which befit God alone. Did not God declare beforehand through the prophets, “I will not give my glory to another”?
Then how do you, being a man, make yourself God? But how does the patient one respond to this?
Quick to show mercy and slow to anger, he bears with those who have become enraged.
He heals their bitterness with his answer, [?] the Scriptures, and brings forward testimonies
to those who act, and does not evade the question. He therefore said, “Have you never heard me
speaking through the prophet: ‘Then you will understand that I am the one who speaks; I have come’?
Or again: ‘From the mouths of nursing infants you have perfected praise, because of your enemies.
You will destroy the enemy and the avenger’? That is what you are—you who read and know the Law and read the prophets,
yet refuse to listen to me, who am proclaimed in the Law and the prophets. For you think, through cunning restraint,
to outwit the glory of God, not understanding that whoever refuses to listen to me also refuses to listen to the Father.
For I came forth from God and entered the world, and my glory is the glory of my Father.”
Thus rebuked by our Savior and God, the foolish stopped arguing,
their mouths having been shut by the truth. But others, stirring up their senseless minds,
plotted against him. But we sing: “Great is our Lord, and great is his strength,
and his understanding is beyond measure.” For all these things happened so that the one who takes away the sin of the world,
the Lamb and Son of God, might willingly come with you to his saving suffering
and be offered for sale. The one who redeems the world with his own life-giving blood
they will value at thirty copper coins. And our Passover will be slaughtered—
Christ, for us—so that those sprinkled with his precious blood, marking their lips like doorposts,
may escape the weapon of the destroyer. And so Christ, who suffered
and rose on the third day, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, in glory and honor—
all creation will worship him. And furthermore, every knee of those in heaven and on earth will bow to him,
and of those under the earth, giving him glory, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
